request.text_before: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife. However little known the feelings or views of such a man may be on his first entering a neighbourhood, this truth is so well fixed in the minds of the surrounding families, that he is considered the rightful property of some one or other of their daughters. "My dear Mr. Bennet," said his lady to him one day, "have you heard that Netherfield Park is let at last?" Mr. Bennet replied that he had not.
request.text_after: "But it is," returned she; "for Mrs. Long has just been here, and she told me all about it." Mr. Bennet made no answer. "Do you not want to know who has taken it?" cried his wife impatiently. "You want to tell me, and I have no objection to hearing it." This was invitation enough.

request.text_before: Mr. Bingley was good-looking and gentlemanlike; his sisters were fine women. His friend Mr. Darcy soon drew the attention of the room by his fine, tall person and the report that he had ten thousand a year. But his manners gave a disgust which turned the tide of his popularity; he was discovered to be proud, to be above his company, and above being pleased. Mr. Bingley urged his friend to dance with Elizabeth Bennet. "She is tolerable, but not handsome enough to tempt me," said Mr. Darcy.
request.text_after: Mr. Darcy walked off, and Elizabeth remained with no very cordial feelings toward him. She told the story with great spirit among her friends, for she had a lively, playful disposition which delighted in anything ridiculous. The evening altogether passed off pleasantly to the whole family. Mrs. Bennet had seen her eldest daughter much admired by the Netherfield party.

request.text_before: It was the Dover road that lay on a Friday night late in November before the first of the persons with whom this history has business. The Dover road lay, as to him, beyond the Dover mail, as it lumbered up Shooter's Hill. A passenger in the mail, Mr. Jarvis Lorry of Tellson's Bank, wrapped to the cheek-bones, was roused when a horseman came up. The messenger handed him a paper. Mr. Lorry read it and said to the man: "Jerry, say that my answer was, RECALLED TO LIFE."
request.text_after: The messenger rode back down the hill, puzzled by the strange reply. "Recalled to life," he muttered. "That's a blazing strange answer, too." Meanwhile Mr. Lorry sat in the coach and let his thoughts wander to a figure long buried, dug out of the ground, and the many faces it might wear.

request.text_before: Call me Ishmael. Some years ago, having little money and nothing particular to interest me on shore, I thought I would sail about a little and see the watery part of the world. Now I came to New Bedford on a Saturday night in December and found that the little packet for Nantucket had already sailed. Walking the dark streets, I came to the Spouter-Inn, kept by one Peter Coffin, and went in out of the cold.
request.text_after: The landlord said the house was full and that I would have to share a bed with a harpooneer who was out selling his head. I did not like the sound of it. I sat by the fire with the sailors and waited, thinking of the narrow passage to the sea and of the whaling voyage I meant to make from Nantucket.

request.text_before: I am by birth a Genevese, and my family is one of the most distinguished of that republic. My father had filled several public situations with honour. When he was nearly forty he married Caroline Beaufort, the daughter of his dead friend. Some years later they travelled to Italy, where my mother saw a poor family and took in a little girl, Elizabeth Lavenza, to be brought up with me. We were called cousins, though she was no blood relation, and I loved her as my own.
request.text_after: My mother's favourite wish was that Elizabeth should one day be my wife. I was the eldest, and we spent the years of our childhood in perfect harmony. Elizabeth was calm and diligent; I had a violent temper and a burning thirst for knowledge. My friend Henry Clerval also lived near us, and he loved stories of chivalry and adventure.

request.text_before: My father's family name being Pirrip, and my christian name Philip, my infant tongue could make of both names nothing longer than Pip. In the bleak churchyard on the marshes a terrible man had seized me, a fearful man, all in coarse grey, with a great iron on his leg. He turned me upside down and made me promise to bring him a file and some wittles. I ran home to the forge, where my sister, Mrs. Joe Gargery, was in a temper, and I stole bread and a pork pie from the pantry.
request.text_after: Next morning I took the file from Joe's tools and the food in my pocket and ran across the misty marshes. I saw two men on the marsh; one was the man I sought, and the other a second convict, whom he attacked, and both fell into a ditch. Then the guns on the prison ships boomed, and Joe said the convicts were being searched for.

request.text_before: Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank. Suddenly a White Rabbit with pink eyes ran close by her, and she heard it say, "Oh dear! I shall be late!" Alice followed it across the field and down a large rabbit-hole. The well was very deep, or she fell very slowly. She found a little glass table with a tiny golden key and a bottle marked DRINK ME. She tasted it and found it very nice.
request.text_after: "What a curious feeling!" said Alice. "I must be shutting up like a telescope." And so it was indeed: she was now only ten inches high, and her face brightened up at the thought that she was now the right size for going through the little door into that lovely garden. But she had left the golden key on the table and could not reach it.

request.text_before: To Sherlock Holmes she is always the woman. A card was handed to Holmes and a tall man in a mask entered Baker Street. He said that he was Count Von Kramm, but Holmes saw through it at once: "I am aware that you are the King of Bohemia." The King confessed that years ago he had known Irene Adler, a famous adventuress, and that she held a photograph of the two of them together. He feared she would send it to the family of his intended bride.
request.text_after: "What does she propose to do with it?" asked Holmes. "To ruin me," said the King. Holmes took notes and asked whether any offer of money had been made. The King said that it had, but she had refused it. Holmes laughed and said he would see him tomorrow at Briony Lodge, where she lived.

request.text_before: I resisted all the way: a new thing for me. Bessie and Miss Abbot grasped my arms and carried me to the red-room, the great chamber where Mr. Reed had died nine years before. Mrs. Reed had ordered it: I was to be locked in for striking my cousin John, who had tormented me. Alone in the cold, solemn room, I saw my own face in the mirror, and a gleam of light crossed the wall, and I thought it was a ghost. I screamed.
request.text_after: Mrs. Reed would not forgive me; she shut me in again. I fell into a kind of fit and woke up in my own bed, with a kind man, the apothecary Mr. Lloyd, looking at me. He asked me whether I should like to go to school. I answered that I should, for I had no happiness in this house.

request.text_before: Jonathan Harker's Journal: I left Munich on May 1st and reached Bistritz, in Transylvania. I am a solicitor sent to the castle of Count Dracula to arrange a purchase of a house in London. The people at the inn crossed themselves and gave me a crucifix. At night a carriage with four black horses and a tall driver in a large hat took me over the Borgo Pass. I saw blue flames flickering in the dark and the wolves howled around the coach.
request.text_after: The Count met me at the great door, an old man, tall, with a long white moustache and cold hands. He bade me welcome and said that I should eat and rest. In the morning I saw that there was no servant in the castle and that he never ate or drank in my presence. I found my bedroom door but I could not see him in the daytime.

request.text_before: Saturday morning had come, and all the summer world was bright. Tom appeared on the sidewalk with a bucket of whitewash and a long-handled brush, and surveyed the fence: thirty yards of board fence nine feet high. Aunt Polly had given him this punishment for his truancy. Then Ben Rogers appeared, munching an apple. Tom went on with his painting as if it were a rare art, and Ben said that he was going swimming.
request.text_after: Presently Ben asked whether he might do some. "Tom, let me whitewash a little," he said, and offered the apple. Tom resisted, and then gave up the brush with reluctance on his face but joy in his heart. By the middle of the afternoon the boys had paid him in marbles, a kite and a dead rat, and the fence had three coats of whitewash.

request.text_before: Squire Trelawney asked me to write down the whole particulars about Treasure Island. I remember the old sea-dog, Billy Bones, who came to the Admiral Benbow inn with his sea-chest and a hand cut across. He sang "Yo-ho-ho, and a bottle of rum," and he told me to keep a weather-eye open for a seafaring man with one leg. He gave me a silver fourpenny every month, and I dreamed of the one-legged man.
request.text_after: He drank a great deal of rum, and told dreadful tales of hangings and storms. The captain was a terror to the whole village. My father was dying at this time, and the old buccaneer was by no means a comfortable guest. I was afraid of him, and of the one-legged sailor he was waiting for.

request.text_before: In my younger and more vulnerable years my father gave me some advice. I am Nick Carraway, and I came East to learn the bond business and rented a small house in West Egg on Long Island, next door to a huge mansion that belonged to a man named Gatsby. One evening I drove across the bay to dine with my cousin Daisy and her husband Tom Buchanan, a brutal man who had been a great football player at New Haven.
request.text_after: Daisy introduced me to Jordan Baker, a golf champion with a cool, insolent manner. Tom took a phone call during dinner and Daisy followed him; Jordan whispered that Tom had a woman in New York. Later, standing on my lawn, I saw a man stretch his arms toward the dark water, toward a single green light at the end of a dock.

request.text_before: It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks were striking thirteen. Winston Smith slipped quickly through the glass doors of Victory Mansions. The hallway smelt of boiled cabbage. On every landing, a poster of an enormous face gazed from the wall: BIG BROTHER IS WATCHING YOU. In his flat the telescreen could not be turned off. Winston, a thirty-nine-year-old Party member who worked at the Ministry of Truth, sat in an alcove and began to write in a diary, a crime in itself.
request.text_after: He remembered the Two Minutes Hate that morning, the face of Emmanuel Goldstein, the enemy of the people, and the sheep-like bleating of the crowd. He felt the dark-haired girl from the Fiction Department staring at him, and wondered whether she was a spy. He wrote, DOWN WITH BIG BROTHER, again and again.

request.book_title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
request.text_before: Harry has lived with the Dursleys for ten years: his aunt Petunia, his uncle Vernon and his cousin Dudley, in the cupboard under the stairs. On Dudley's birthday the family takes Harry along to the zoo. In the reptile house a boa constrictor winks at Harry, and he speaks to it, and the glass vanishes. Dudley falls into the tank and the snake slithers out, thanking Harry in a hiss. Harry is punished and locked in his cupboard again.
request.text_after: Harry lay awake thinking about the snake, which had said it had never been to Brazil. He did not know how he had made the glass disappear. He thought about the strange things that had always happened around him, such as the time his hair grew back overnight after Aunt Petunia cut it short.

request.text_before: In a hole in the ground there lived a hobbit. Bilbo Baggins was quiet and well-off, and had never had an adventure. One morning Gandalf, a wizard, passed by and said he was looking for someone to share in an adventure. That evening, to Bilbo's alarm, thirteen dwarves arrived at his door one by one, Thorin Oakenshield last of all, and ate his pantry empty. The dwarves sang of the Lonely Mountain and the hoard of gold they had lost.
request.text_after: Gandalf produced a map and a key that had belonged to Thorin's father. The dwarves discussed their plan to reclaim their treasure and wanted a burglar for the job. Bilbo felt a Tookish stirring, but he was afraid, and went to bed with a headache. In the morning he found them gone, and a note on the mantelpiece.

request.text_before: At half-past ten that night, Tom and Huckleberry Finn crept out to meet at the old graveyard, carrying a dead cat. They hid behind the elms and waited in the dark. Soon they saw three men coming with a lantern: Muff Potter, Injun Joe, and young Doctor Robinson, who had come to dig up a grave. The boys held their breath.
request.text_after: The men took up the body and put it in a wheelbarrow. Injun Joe demanded more money, and Potter and Joe quarrelled with the doctor. The doctor struck Potter down with a headboard, and Injun Joe snatched Potter's knife and drove it into the doctor's chest, killing him, and then put the knife in the hand of the unconscious Potter.

request.text_before: It was on a dreary night of November that I beheld the accomplishment of my toils. With an anxiety that almost amounted to agony, I collected the instruments of life around me, that I might infuse a spark of being into the lifeless thing that lay at my feet. It was already one in the morning; the rain pattered dismally against the panes, and my candle was nearly burnt out.
request.text_after: When, by the glimmer of the half-extinguished light, I saw the dull yellow eye of the creature open; it breathed hard, and a convulsive motion agitated its limbs. I rushed out of the room and ran up and down my bedchamber, unable to compose my mind to sleep. Then I fell into a dream, and saw Elizabeth, and held her in my arms, and she became the corpse of my mother.

request.text_before: As the Hispaniola lay at anchor off the island, the crew was in a lively mood. I was sent to the apple barrel to get an apple, and there was so little left that I climbed in and sat down in the dark, and began to eat. Then the sleepiness got the better of me, and I was almost asleep when a heavy man sat down against the barrel with a thump. It was the voice of Long John Silver, and I began to listen.
request.text_after: Silver was talking to a young sailor, Dick Johnson. He said that he had been quartermaster under Flint, and that the whole crew was his and would take the ship. He said that Captain Smollett and the squire and the doctor were to be killed at the right moment. I lay in the barrel trembling, learning that the cook and half the crew were pirates and had planned a mutiny.

request.text_before: Jonathan Harker's Journal: I woke early and felt that I was a prisoner in the castle. The doors were locked, and the Count was never to be seen by day. I explored the castle at night, and at last I found a door that was open, down a steep winding stair, into an old ruined chapel with great vaults of earth and a number of old coffins.
request.text_after: In one of the boxes, on a bed of newly dug earth, lay the Count. He seemed half-dead, or half asleep; his eyes were open and stony, and there was no pulse and no breath. There was a mocking smile on his face, and blood at his lips. I fled in horror, and thought of the three women who had come to me in the moonlight.

request.text_before: At Thornfield I heard a strange laugh in the third storey, low, suppressed and deep. Grace Poole, the seamstress, was said to be the one who laughed, but I was not satisfied. One night, soon after, I was woken by a demoniac laugh close to my door. I rose and looked out and saw a candle on the floor and the smell of burning.
request.text_after: I rushed into Mr. Rochester's room and found the bed curtains in flames and Mr. Rochester sunk in deep sleep, with the fire all about him. I threw water on him and the bed, and woke him. He said it was one of Grace Poole's tricks and asked me to say nothing, and went up to the third storey himself with a candle.

request.book_title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
request.text_before: In Ollivander's wand shop, Harry tries wand after wand: beech, ebony, maple, and each time Mr. Ollivander takes the wand back with a muttered 'No, not that one.' The shop is dusty and narrow. Hagrid waits outside with an owl. Mr. Ollivander says that the wand chooses the wizard, and he recalls selling wands to Harry's parents.
request.text_after: At last Harry takes a holly wand with a phoenix feather, eleven inches. A stream of red and gold sparks shoots out. Mr. Ollivander says that the phoenix gave one other feather, and that the wand which gave Harry his scar was its brother, and that the person who owned it did great but terrible things.

request.text_before: "Why, my dear, you must know, Mrs. Long says that Netherfield is taken by a young man of large fortune from the north of England; that he came down on Monday in a chaise and four to see the place, and was so much delighted with it that he agreed with Mr. Morris immediately." "What is his name?" "Bingley." "Is he married or single?" "Oh, single, my dear! A single man of large fortune; four or five thousand a year. What a fine thing for our girls!"
"Curiouser and curiouser!" cried Alice.
request.text_after: She was so much surprised that for the moment she quite forgot how to speak good English. "Now I'm opening out like the largest telescope that ever was! Good-bye, feet!" Just then her head struck against the roof of the hall, and she took up the little golden key and hurried to the garden door.

request.text_before: Queequeg was a native of Kokovoko, an island far away to the West and South. I sat by him on the bed and he took out his tomahawk pipe, and smoked it, and passed it to me. We were soon friends, and he put his arm round me, and I slept soundly. The next morning we left the inn together and walked down to the wharf to take the packet to Nantucket.
request.text_after: On the wharf I spoke of the three whaling ships in the harbour: the Devil-Dam, the Tit-bit and the Pequod. Queequeg said he would choose by his idol Yojo, and so we went aboard the Pequod, to find the captain.

request.text_before: The Caterpillar and Alice looked at each other for some time in silence. At last the Caterpillar took the hookah out of its mouth and said in a languid, sleepy voice, "Who are you?" "I hardly know, sir, just at present," said Alice. She told it about her size changing and the caterpillar told her that one side of the mushroom would make her grow taller and the other shorter.
request.text_after: She nibbled the right-hand bit and her chin struck her foot. She bit a little of the left-hand piece and her neck stretched like a serpent above the trees. A pigeon cried "Serpent!" and she explained that she was a little girl.

request.text_before: जुम्मन शेख और अलगू चौधरी में गाढ़ी मित्रता थी। साझेमें खेती होती थी। कुछ लेन-देनमें भी साझा था। एकको दूसरेपर अटल विश्वास था। जुम्मनकी एक बूढ़ी खाला थी, जिसके पास कुछ थोड़ी-सी मिलकियत थी। उसने अपनी जायदाद जुम्मनके नाम लिख दी। जब तक दानपत्र न लिखा गया था, तब तक खालाजानकी खूब खातिरदारी होती रही।
request.text_after: दानपत्र रजिस्ट्री हो जानेके बाद खालाजानके साथ व्यवहार बदल गया। रोटीके साथ कड़वी बातें मिलने लगीं। बूढ़ी खालाने कई बार जुम्मनसे कहा, पर उसने टालमटोल की। अन्तमें खाला तंग आ गई और उसने कहा कि मैं पंचायत बुलाऊँगी।

request.text_before: होरीराम ने दोनों बैलोंको सानी-पानी देकर अपनी स्त्री धनियासे कहा, गोबरको भेज देना, मैं रायसाहबके पास जा रहा हूँ। धनियाने कहा कि इतनी सुबह क्यों जा रहे हो। होरीने कहा कि रायसाहबसे मिलना जरूरी है, नहीं तो बेदखली हो जाएगी। उसे गायकी बड़ी लालसा थी, और वह सोचता था कि दरवाजेपर गाय बँध जाए तो मरजादा बढ़ जाए।
request.text_after: रास्तेमें होरीको भोलाराम मिला, जो गायें बेचता था। भोलाने अपनी एक दुधारू गाय उधार देनेकी बात कही। होरीका मन ललचा गया, पर उसने कहा कि वह घर लौटकर सोचेगा। धनियाने सुना तो खुश भी हुई और डरी भी।

request.text_before: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife. "My dear Mr. Bennet," said his lady to him one day, "have you heard that Netherfield Park is let at last?" Mr. Bennet replied that he had not. "But it is," returned she; "for Mrs. Long has just been here."
request.text_after: "Do you not want to know who has taken it?" cried his wife impatiently. "You want to tell me, and I have no objection to hearing it." This was invitation enough. "A young man of large fortune from the north of England has taken it."

request.text_before: Ilse folded the map along the old creases and looked at the harbour. The tide had left salt on every rope. Her uncle would not speak of the third survey, and the clerk at the customs house had stopped meeting her eyes. She decided she would take the ferry before dawn.
request.text_after: On the ferry a man in a green coat asked her whether she was the one who had drawn the northern chart. She said she was not, and he smiled in a way she did not like.

request.text_before: The snow had closed the road to Varn by the time Corin reached the inn. He counted the coins in his glove and ordered soup. The innkeeper said that the copper gate had not been opened since the autumn, and that nobody who asked about it stayed long.
request.text_after: Corin finished his soup and went to the window. Across the white yard a lamp burned in the stable, and somebody moved behind it, carrying something long wrapped in cloth.

request.text_before: Marguerite stood on the pier with the letter in her hand. The fishing boats were out, and the wind carried the smell of smoke from the cannery. She read the last line again. Her sister had signed it with the name they had used as children.
request.text_after: She folded the letter into her coat and walked back along the pier. At the end of it, the harbourmaster was talking to two strangers in dark coats, and he lifted his hand when he saw her.

request.book_title: My Year of Tuesdays: A Garden Diary
request.text_before: Tuesday, March 4. Planted the first row of peas. The soil was still cold and my knees complained. The neighbour's cat sat on the compost bin and watched me with open contempt. I wrote the names of the seed packets in the back of this notebook so I would not forget.
request.text_after: Tuesday, March 11. It rained all day. I spent the afternoon repotting the tomato seedlings on the windowsill and reading old seed catalogues. The radio said the frost would return on Thursday.

request.text_before: Action items from Monday's meeting: finalize the vendor shortlist, review the draft budget with finance, and confirm the launch date with the regional leads. The team agreed that the dashboard migration should be tracked separately.
request.text_after: Open questions: who owns the support rota in December? Does the budget include the extra licences? Next meeting is on Thursday at ten.

request.text_before: सुबह की धूप आँगन में उतर आई थी। मीरा ने पुरानी चाभी को हथेली पर रखकर देखा। नीले दरवाज़े पर जंग लग चुका था। दादी कहती थीं कि इस दरवाज़े के पीछे कोई नहीं जाता।
request.text_after: उसने चाभी ताले में डाली तो ताला हल्की-सी आवाज़ के साथ घूम गया। पीछे से किसी ने उसका नाम पुकारा।
